resumen_original: Abstract Objective To evaluate the effect of rutin extracted from Dimorphandra gardneriana on the tensile strength and color changes of demineralized dentin collagen. Methods Two independent experiments were conducted using 244 sound human third molars. For quantitative color analysis, 204 teeth were used to prepare 204 dentin discs, which were allocated to 12 groups (n = 17). For tensile strength analysis, 40 teeth were used to prepare 120 rectangular dentin specimens, which were allocated to 12 groups (n = 10). Specimens were completely demineralized in 10% phosphoric acid and treated with distilled water (control) or aqueous rutin solutions (0.004%, 0.008%, or 0.0125%) for 1, 30, or 60 min. Color changes (ΔL*, Δa*, Δb*, and ΔE*ab) were assessed spectrophotometrically before and after biomodification, and tensile strength was measured using a universal testing machine. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA followed by the Student–Newman–Keuls test when significant effects were detected (α = 0.05). Results No significant effects of treatment, biomodification time, or their interaction were observed for ΔL*, Δa*, Δb*, or ΔE*ab (p > 0.05). Rutin-treated specimens showed significantly higher tensile strength than control specimens (p < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were observed among the rutin concentrations (p > 0.05). Neither biomodification time nor the treatment × time interaction significantly affected tensile strength (p > 0.05). Conclusions Within the limitations of this in vitro study, rutin increased the immediate tensile strength of demineralized dentin collagen, whereas no significant differences in color change were observed among the treatments under the conditions evaluated. titulo_original: Effects of low-pressure non-thermal oxygen plasma treatments on mechanical properties of a PMMA resin for denture base
resumen_original: Abstract Aim To evaluate the mechanical properties of a denture base resin after repeated exposure to an alternative disinfection treatment using low-pressure non-thermal oxygen plasma (O₂ NTP). Materials and methods For each assay, the resin (ProBase® Hot, Ivoclar) samples were prepared using the heat-compression mold technique. They were exposed to one or six low-pressure or O2 NTP treatments for 120 min (n = 10/group). Dimensional stability, surface hardness, flexural strength and elastic modulus were evaluated before and after low pressure and O2 NTP treatments. SEM was used to observe the effect of the different treatments on the samples. Statistical analyses were performed using Student’s t-test or one-way ANOVA followed by a Tukey’s post hoc test according to the Shapiro-Wilk test normal distribution analysis (p < 0.05). Results No adverse effects on the dimensional stability and surface hardness were noted after repeated O2 NTP treatments. Flexural strength and elastic modulus were not significantly altered only if the resin was dehydrated under the controlled dry condition of this study. Indeed, SEM images revealed cracks on the samples surfaces only when moisture remained in the resin prior to plasma exposure. Conclusion O2 NTP could be a promising alternative approach to disinfect dentures, provided the resin’s hydration state is strictly controlled. resumen_original: Abstract Aims To describe patient-reported comfort and satisfaction and clinical team experience during surgical extraction of mandibular third molars under local anaesthesia within a single oral surgery service, with and without the use of OptraGate, a self-retaining retractor. Materials and methods Over six months, 100 patients undergoing surgical extraction of lower third molars were invited to complete a post-operative questionnaire assessing comfort and satisfaction. 50 patients underwent extraction using conventional-retraction techniques, and 50 underwent extraction using OptraGate alongside a Minnesota retractor. Clinicians and nursing staff completed a separate questionnaire assessing visibility, retraction, procedural time, and overall satisfaction. The project received approval from the Barts Health NHS Trust Information Governance and Clinical Effectiveness Teams. Allocation to each group was based on the treating clinician’s preference for that procedure, rather than randomisation. Results A higher proportion of patients in the OptraGate group reported comfort (80% vs 64%) and satisfaction (80% vs 56%) than those in the conventional group. Clinician- and nurse-reported visibility and retraction were rated as neutral, good, or excellent in 25% of procedures without OptraGate, compared with 89% of procedures with OptraGate. A perceived reduction in surgical time was reported in 78% of OptraGate cases, and 76% of surgical-team evaluations reported very high overall satisfaction. Conclusions Within this service, a higher proportion of patients reported comfort and satisfaction, and the clinical team reported a more favourable experience when OptraGate was used during third molar surgery. titulo_original: Full (total) pulpotomy versus non-surgical root canal treatment for irreversible pulpitis: a human-led umbrella review with AI-assisted appraisal
resumen_original: Abstract Objective To evaluate systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing vital pulp treatments (VPTs) with non-surgical root canal treatment (NSRCT) for irreversible pulpitis (IP) in permanent teeth, focusing on clinical/radiographic success and postoperative pain, and to compare AI (ChatGPT-4.1) with human reviewers for risk of bias (ROBIS) and methodological quality (AMSTAR-2). Materials and Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, EBSCO and Google Scholar were searched from inception to January 2026 according to PRISMA 2020. Predefined criteria guided screening and extraction. Two reviewers independently applied AMSTAR-2 and ROBIS; the same appraisals were repeated with ChatGPT-4.1 using identical inputs. Results Of 641 records, 12 systematic reviews met the eligibility criteria; six incorporated quantitative synthesis/meta-analysis, whereas the remaining reviews used structured qualitative synthesis. Regarding the outcomes assessed, 2 reviews focused on postoperative pain, 7 on clinical/radiographic success, and 3 addressed both. All compared only one VPT technique -full pulpotomy- with NSRCT; no eligible reviews provided outcomes for other VPTs. The evidence ultimately drew on 11 unique primary studies. Across reviews, full pulpotomy often achieved short- to medium-term outcomes comparable to NSRCT. Human AMSTAR-2 ratings were 1 critically low, 8 low, 1 moderate, and 2 high; human–ChatGPT-4.1 agreement was moderate-to-substantial. For AMSTAR-2 overall confidence, agreement was 66.7% (κ = 0.529; quadratic weighted κ = 0.824), while for ROBIS overall risk it was 83.3% (κ = 0.636). Disagreements mainly involved AMSTAR-2 Q7/Q10 and ROBIS Domains 1/3. Conclusion Full pulpotomy may be a less invasive alternative to NSRCT in selected IP cases, but certainty is constrained by the small and overlapping primary evidence base. Although eligibility criteria covered other VPT modalities, no eligible randomized evidence comparing partial pulpotomy or direct pulp capping with NSRCT was identified. Future randomized clinical trials should evaluate not only full pulpotomy but also other VPT approaches using standardized diagnostic, procedural, and outcome criteria. AI may support structured appraisal, but should augment rather than replace expert judgment. titulo_original: Effectiveness of digitally fabricated versus conventional stabilizing splints in temporomandibular disorders: a randomized controlled trial protocol
resumen_original: Abstract Background Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) comprise a group of conditions affecting the muscles and temporomandibular joints of the stomatognathic system and may result in pain, joint dysfunction, and impaired mandibular function. Stabilization splints are commonly used as a conservative treatment modality for TMD. Conventional splint fabrication using heat-cured acrylic resin is technique-sensitive and may be associated with variability in fabrication and clinical adjustment. Digital workflows incorporating computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM), followed by additive manufacturing, may improve standardization, reproducibility, and fabrication accuracy. However, clinical evidence directly comparing digitally fabricated and conventionally fabricated stabilization splints remains limited. Participants and methodology This single-center, two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will compare digitally fabricated and conventionally fabricated maxillary stabilization splints. A total of 120 participants aged 18–40 years with temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthralgia diagnosed according to the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD) axis I will be recruited and randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the digital or conventional stabilization splint group. All splints will have standardized design, coverage, thickness, and occlusal characteristics. Outcome assessment will be performed by a blinded assessor. The primary outcome is the change in Characteristic Pain Intensity (CPI; 0–100) from baseline to 3 months. Secondary outcomes include pain-related disability, maximum unassisted mouth opening, jaw functional limitation, temporomandibular joint clicking, oral health-related quality of life, and splint compliance. Participants will be analyzed according to their original randomized allocation, irrespective of treatment adherence or discontinuation. The primary outcome will be analyzed using linear mixed-effects modeling, including treatment group, time, and treatment-by-time interaction. Discussion This trial aims to provide clinical evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of digitally fabricated and conventionally fabricated stabilization splints for the management of TMD. The findings may inform evidence-based selection of splint fabrication workflows and help determine whether the potential advantages of digital fabrication translate into comparable or improved clinical outcomes. titulo_original: Long-term stability and effectiveness of maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis
resumen_original: Abstract Objective Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) surgery has been shown to effectively increase airway volume and reduce apnoea severity in adult patients with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). This study aimed to evaluate the long-term stability and effectiveness of MMA in managing OSA. Methods Following PROSPERO registration (CRD42021238944), major databases and grey literature were searched through May 2025 for studies with ≥2-year follow-up. The review was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomised Studies (MINORS). Meta-analyses were performed on skeletal parameters, Sella-Nasion-Point A (SNA) and Sella-Nasion-Point B (SNB) angles, and the Apnoea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). The certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results Of 1299 articles retrieved, 34 underwent full-text review, and 14 met the inclusion criteria. Assessment using the MINORS tool revealed moderate concerns in a few studies, while the overall certainty of evidence was downgraded to low. Meta-analysis showed significant post-operative skeletal changes: SNA angle increased by a mean of 6.29° (95% CI: 4.90–7.67°) and remained stable at 6.18° (95% CI: 4.86–7.51°) during long-term follow-up. SNB increased by 4.80° (95% CI: 3.15–6.45°) and remained stable at 5.38° (95% CI: 3.04–7.71°). AHI decreased significantly by 40.30 events/hour (95% CI: 32.23–48.37) in the long term. Conclusion MMA surgery was associated with substantial long-term improvement in AHI and generally stable skeletal outcomes among adult OSA patients. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity and the low certainty of evidence limit the precision and generalisability of the pooled estimates. Further well-designed prospective studies with standardised reporting and long-term follow-up are warranted. resumen_original: Abstract Background Patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) planned for radiotherapy (RT) frequently require pre-treatment dental extractions. Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a serious late complication of RT. Maximising the extent of socket healing before RT commences is critical to the prevention of ORN. Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) concentrates autologous growth factors and may accelerate socket healing. Purpose To analyse the literature and identify whether PRF supports earlier healing or reduced incidence of ORN. Study design, setting, sample This systematic review evaluates clinical evidence for PRF in dental extraction sockets in patients with planned or prior head and neck RT. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and the HaNDLE-on-QoL database were searched from database inception to December 2025. Predictor/Exposure/Independent variable Studies of any design evaluating PRF in extraction sockets of patients with HNC receiving or planned for RT were eligible. Main outcome variable(s) The primary outcome variables were time to healing and incidence of ORN. Covariates Covariates were assessed based on reporting in individual studies. Analysis Studies were assessed for methodological robustness, including the PRISMA 2020 framework. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (RoB) 2.0 tool. Results Two primary studies, both randomised controlled trials (RCTs), met the inclusion criteria for the qualitative synthesis; one systematic review with meta-analysis was retained separately as contextual evidence. Neither RCT demonstrated a statistically significant benefit over conventional socket management. The single systematic review identified only one eligible PRF study (n = 11), precluding meta-analysis. No studies were conducted in the pre-RT setting. Conclusions Current evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine use of PRF for ORN prevention in this population. Critically, both RCTs were substantially underpowered and at high risk of type II error. Both studied only post-irradiated patients and administered antibiotics to every participant in both arms, which is likely to have suppressed the baseline ORN event rate. No pre-RT evidence exists, despite this representing the most clinically and biologically relevant scenario. Adequately powered, multicentre RCTs in the pre-RT setting are required. titulo_original: Comparative success of restorative techniques for pulpectomy in primary teeth: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
resumen_original: Abstract Background To date, there is no consensus on which restorative strategy provides the greatest success for primary teeth undergoing endodontic treatment. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effect of different restorative techniques on the success of pulpectomy in primary teeth. Methods: Two reviewers conducted searches in MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and grey literature databases up to January 2026. Prospective studies evaluating restorations in primary teeth treated with pulpectomy were included. Studies that did not report the success rate of pulpectomy treatment or that involved specific patient groups were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using ROB 2.0 and ROBINS-I. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed to compare pulpectomy success among restorative techniques, and the certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Results: Of 2161 records identified, seven studies were included in the systematic review. Three studies involving five restorative strategies were included in the network meta-analysis. No statistically significant differences were observed between any of the restorative strategies in the network meta-analysis. Treatment ranking based on SUCRA values indicated that stainless steel crowns (SSC) ranked highest (SUCRA = 73.13%), followed by composite resin (CR; 69.95%), compomer (55.13%), amalgam (39.34%), and resin-modified glass ionomer cement (RMGIC; 12.45%). Conclusion: The available evidence does not support the superiority of one restorative strategy over another for pulpectomized primary teeth. Given the methodological limitations of the available studies and the moderate to very low certainty of the evidence, further well-designed studies are needed to establish the most effective restorative approach. resumen_original: Abstract Aim This systematic review aimed to summarize the factors that can influence the success rate of restoration repair. Methods A search was carried out in the PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science and ProQuest databases in January 2026. Inclusion criteria were randomised controlled trials (RCTs) or non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs) with data on restoration repair; and exclusion criteria were follow-up less than 12 months, loss to follow-up higher than 30%, studies, evaluating anterior teeth and unclear evaluation criteria. The risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool for RCTs and ROBINS-I for NRSIs, and the certainty of evidence with the GRADE tool. A single-arm meta-analysis assessed the pooled proportion (95% CI) of repair success rates. Subgroup meta-analyses were also performed. Results Ten studies were included in the final qualitative and quantitative synthesis; however, only seven studies (five RCTs and two NRSIs) were eligible for meta-analysis after stratification by follow-up time. The studies included 302 participants and 542 repaired restorations. The most consistently reported follow-up periods for quantitative analysis were 24 and 120 months. The estimated overall success rates ranged from 78% (95% CI: 67 to 88) in RCTs to 82% (95% CI: 57 to 100) in NRSIs. Discussion No factors were identified as significantly influencing repair success, likely reflecting the limited number of studies and the substantial heterogeneity of the available evidence. Most RCTs presented some concerns regarding risk of bias, especially related to study registration and deviations from intended interventions. Among NRSIs, risk of bias varied from low to moderate due to missing data. Only studies involving permanent teeth were eligible. Interpretation of these findings is limited by the low to very low certainty of the evidence, the small number of eligible studies, substantial methodological heterogeneity, and imprecision of the pooled estimates. Conclusion Although the available evidence suggests favourable long-term outcomes for retoration repair in permanent teeth, the low to very-low certainty of evidence and substancial heterogeneity limit confidence in these findings. Further well-designed studies are needed to clarify the determinants of repair outcomes and strengthen evidence-based clinical decision-making. Access options Subscribe to this journal

resumen_original: Introduction Orthodontics is experiencing a major paradigm shift driven by digital technologies, 3D printing, advanced clear aligners, and comprehensive virtual workflows (–). Modern orthodontic patients increasingly seek treatment options that combine high aesthetic discretion and physiological comfort with optimal clinical outcomes and chairside efficiency (–). To rigorously evaluate the clinical efficacy, biomechanical force mechanics, diagnostic accuracy, and environmental sustainability of these evolving modalities, the Research Topic “Emerging Technologies in Orthodontic Treatments: 3D Printing, Clear Aligners, and Beyond” was convened in Frontiers in Dental Medicine (Reconstructive Dentistry section), in collaboration with Frontiers in Materials (Biomaterials and Bio-Inspired Materials) and Frontiers in Oral Health (Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery). This collective Research Topic brings together 8 primary research articles, systematic reviews, and technical innovations contributed by 34 authors. The collection establishes a multi-faceted platform designed to optimize force delivery systems, refine 3D digital manufacturing, enhance surgical precision, advance preclinical education, and establish ecological stewardship in modern dental practice. Additive manufacturing, 3D-printed aligners, and precision surgical guidance A major thematic focus of this collection centers on the clinical application and biomechanical performance of 3D printing in appliance fabrication. Traditional aligner manufacturing relies on indirect thermoforming over printed physical working models, a process known to cause material degradation, variable wall thickness, and microstructural stress relaxation (, ). Direct additive manufacturing addresses these limitations by eliminating physical model production, offering superior geometric control, custom thickness distribution, and reduced plastic waste (). resumen_original: A study published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases with Biotia, Bumrungrad International Hospital, and Chulalongkorn University finds that pathogen identification combined with resistance interpretation is what could turn the result into a treatment decision. NEW YORK, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A metagenomic sequencing report could have changed the antibiotic decision in 4 out of 10 initial prescriptions for urinary tract infections (UTIs), according to a peer-reviewed study published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. The report could have flagged antibiotics likely to fail and identified patients who could step down from broad-spectrum drugs. The study was a collaboration between Bumrungrad International Hospital, Chulalongkorn University, and Biotia. It evaluated Biotia's bioinformatics software, BIOTIA-DX, on sequencing data from urine samples collected at a tertiary hospital in Bangkok, Thailand – a setting where antibiotic resistance in uropathogens is high. "Antimicrobial resistance is one of the defining health challenges of our time, and every antibiotic decision matters. This study moves the conversation beyond whether sequencing can find a pathogen to whether it can help doctors choose the right treatment sooner. We're proud to have done this work with our partners at Bumrungrad and Chulalongkorn", said Niamh O'Hara, PhD, the CEO and Co-Founder of Biotia. UTIs are among the most common reasons antibiotics are prescribed. Because standard culture results are often followed by susceptibility testing, the results can take several days to return, requiring doctors to start treatment without knowing the pathogen or its resistance profile. That gap puts patients at risk of ineffective treatment and fuels the spread of drug resistance, and the possibility of infections that have no treatment options. In this study, researchers compared BIOTIA-DX results with standard culture and susceptibility testing in 251 urine samples collected from symptomatic patients. They then examined 54 antibiotic prescriptions written on the day each sample was collected, to ask whether a same-day metagenomic report would have changed the clinical treatment decision. resumen_original: Près de quarante ans après la mise en place de leurs implants, les patients demeurent extrêmement satisfaits de leur fonction, malgré une appréciation plus contrastée de leur rendu esthétique. C’est la principale conclusion d’une étude suédoise publiée le 21 octobre dernier dans Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research , qui offre l’un des reculs les plus longs jamais rapportés sur des traitements implantaires. Ces résultats revêtent une portée particulière. Les patients étudiés ont été traités entre 1982 et 1985 à l’Université de Göteborg, berceau des travaux du professeur Per-Ingvar Brånemark, dont les recherches sur l’ostéointégration ont jeté les bases de l’implantologie moderne. Cette situation unique permet aujourd’hui aux chercheurs de documenter le devenir clinique et le ressenti des patients près de quatre décennies après la pose des implants. L’étude fait suite à des travaux publiés en 2025 montrant que les 18 implants retrouvés chez ces patients étaient toujours en fonction après près de 40 ans. Les chercheurs ont cette fois cherché à évaluer le point de vue des patients eux-mêmes. Treize d’entre eux ont répondu à des questionnaires portant sur leur satisfaction globale, la fonction masticatoire, l’esthétique des restaurations et leur qualité de vie liée à la santé orale. Les résultats sont particulièrement favorables sur le plan fonctionnel. Sur une échelle de 0 à 100, les patients ont attribué une note moyenne de 93 au résultat global du traitement et de 96 à sa fonction malgré le temps écoulé. Les patients notent également un impact limité de leur état bucco-dentaire sur leur qualité de vie quotidienne. L’analyse esthétique apparaît en revanche plus nuancée.
